en: Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to me: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from Shu'bah, who said: I heard Sulayman saying: I heard Abu Sufyan saying: I heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: Ubayy was struck by an arrow on the Day of the Confederates on his medial arm vein, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) cauterized it.

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us; (Second chain) and Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman informed us: Sufyan informed us; both from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission, and neither of them mentioned: "so he severed a vein of his."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—Yahya said—and the wording is his: informed us, and the other two said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent a physician to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, so he severed a vein of his and then cauterized it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (Second chain) and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: that Umm Salamah asked permission of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to be cupped, so the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered Abu Taybah to cup her. He said: I think he said: he was her foster brother through breastfeeding or a boy who had not reached puberty.

Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to me: my father narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, who said: Jabir ibn Abdillah came to our family while a man among us was complaining of an ulcer or a wound. He asked: "What ails you?" The man said: "An ulcer that has caused me great hardship." Jabir said: "O boy, bring me a cupper." The man said to him: "What will you do with a cupper, O Abu Abdillah?" He said: "I want to apply a cupping glass to it." The man said: "By Allah, even if a fly touches it, or my garment brushes against it, it hurts me and causes me hardship!" When Jabir saw his aversion to that, he said: "Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'If there is good in any of your remedies, it is in the incision of a cupper, or a drink of honey, or cauterization with fire.' And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'And I do not like to be cauterized.'" He said: So he brought a cupper who lanced it, and that which he was suffering went away.

Harun ibn Ma'ruf and Abu al-Tahir narrated to us—they said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Amr informed me that Bukayr narrated to him that Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to him that Jabir ibn Abdillah visited al-Muqanna' during his illness and then said: "I will not leave until you are cupped, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'Indeed, in it there is healing.'"

Harun ibn Ma'ruf, Abu al-Tahir, and Ahmad ibn Isa narrated to us—they said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Amr—and he is Ibn al-Harith—informed me, from Abd Rabbihi ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "For every disease there is a cure, so when the cure for the disease is applied, the person is cured by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Sublime."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Sufyan informed us, from Sa'id al-Jurayri: Yazid ibn Abdillah ibn al-Shikhkhir narrated to us, from Uthman ibn Abi al-As al-Thaqafi, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah..." then he mentioned the like of their hadith.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Salim ibn Nuh narrated to us; (Second chain) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; both of them from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Ala', from Uthman ibn Abi al-As, that he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he mentioned the like of it, but he did not mention "three times" in the hadith of Salim ibn Nuh.

Yahya ibn Khalaf al-Bahili narrated to us: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Ala': that Uthman ibn Abi al-As came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Satan has intervened between me and my prayer and my recitation, confusing it for me." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "That is a devil called Khinzab. So when you perceive him, seek refuge with Allah from him and spit lightly to your left three times." He said: I did that, and Allah dispelled him from me.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed me, from Uthman ibn Abi al-As al-Thaqafi, that he complained to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) of a pain he had felt in his body since he became Muslim. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "Place your hand on the part of your body that hurts and say, 'In the Name of Allah' three times, and say seven times: 'I seek refuge with Allah and His power from the evil of what I find and dread.'"

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, similar to it, except that he said: "So a man from among us stood up with her whom we had never known to perform incantations."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from his brother Ma'bad ibn Sirin, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: We halted at a campsite, and a woman came to us and said: "The chief of the tribe has been stung by a scorpion; is there any reciter of incantations among you?" A man from among us went with her whom we did not think knew how to recite incantations. He recited the Opening of the Book over him, and he was cured. They gave him some sheep and gave us milk to drink. We said: "Did you know how to perform incantations?" He said: "I only treated him with the Opening of the Book." He said: I said: "Do not touch them until we go to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." So we came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and mentioned that to him. He said: "And how did he know that it was an incantation? Distribute them, and assign a share for me along with you."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us, both from Ghundar Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, with this chain of transmission, and he said in the hadith: "He began reciting the Mother of the Quran, gathering his saliva and spitting lightly, and the man was cured."

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that some people among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) were on a journey. They passed by a clan among the Arab clans and requested hospitality from them, but they refused to host them. They then said to them: "Is there any reciter of incantations among you, for the chief of the clan has been stung or afflicted?" A man from among them said: "Yes." So he came to him and treated him with the Opening of the Book, and the man was cured. He was given a flock of sheep, but he refused to accept it, saying: "Not until I mention this to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." So he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and mentioned that to him, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I did not recite over him anything except the Opening of the Book." The Prophet smiled and said: "And what made you know that it is an incantation?" Then he said: "Take them from them, and assign a share for me along with you."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who said: We used to recite incantations in the Pre-Islamic Period of Ignorance, so we said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is your view concerning that?" He said: "Present your incantations to me. There is no harm in incantations as long as they contain no polytheism."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade incantations. Then the family of Amr ibn Hazm came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we had an incantation with which we used to treat scorpion stings, but you have forbidden incantations." He said: So they presented it to him. He said: "I see no harm in it. Whoever among you is able to benefit his brother, let him benefit him."
Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us—they said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: I had a maternal uncle who used to perform incantations for scorpion stings, but the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade incantations. He said: So he went to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have forbidden incantations, and I perform incantations for scorpion stings." He said: "Whoever among you is able to benefit his brother, let him do so."

Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to me: my father narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, except that he said: A man from the people said: "Shall I perform an incantation for him, O Messenger of Allah?" and he did not say "Shall I perform an incantation?"

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) granted permission for the incantation against snakebite to Banu Amr. Abu al-Zubayr said: And I heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: A scorpion stung a man among us while we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I recite an incantation?" He said: "Whoever among you is able to benefit his brother, let him do so."

Uqbah ibn Mukram al-Ammi narrated to me: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: and Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) granted a concession to the family of Hazm for the incantation against snakebite, and he said to Asma' bint Umays: "Why do I see the bodies of my brother's sons so emaciated? Has destitution afflicted them?" She said: "No, but the evil eye hastens toward them." He said: "Recite incantations over them." She said: "So I presented them to him, and he said: 'Recite incantations over them.'"

Abu al-Rabi' Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Zubaydi narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said regarding a young girl in the house of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—seeing a discoloration on her face—he said: "She is affected by an evil eye, so seek an incantation for her"—meaning a paleness in her face.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sufyan; (Second chain) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: Hasan—and he is Ibn Salih—narrated to us; both of them from Asim, from Yusuf ibn Abdillah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) granted a concession for incantations against the evil eye, venomous stings, and skin rashes. And in the hadith of Sufyan: Yusuf ibn Abdillah ibn al-Harith.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Yusuf ibn Abdillah, from Anas ibn Malik, regarding incantations; he said: "A concession was granted for venomous stings, skin rashes, and the evil eye."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'bad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Shaddad, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to command me to seek an incantation against the evil eye.
Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us: Mis'ar narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: informed us, and Abu Bakr and Abu Kurayb said—and the wording is theirs: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Mis'ar: Ma'bad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Ibn Shaddad, from A'ishah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to command her to seek an incantation against the evil eye.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us—and the wording is that of Ibn Abi Umar—they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abd Rabbihi ibn Sa'id, from Amrah, from A'ishah: that whenever a person suffered from an ailment, or had an ulcer or a wound, the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would gesture with his finger like this—and Sufyan placed his forefinger on the ground and then raised it: "In the name of Allah, the dust of our earth mixed with the saliva of one of us, so that our sick may be healed, by the permission of our Lord." Ibn Abi Shaybah said: "may be healed," and Zuhayr said: "so that our sick may be healed."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) granted a concession to a household among the Ansar to recite incantations for venomous stings.
